o.text: A derivation from Proto-Turkic *tẹg- (“to cost, to be worth, etc”), whence also dəymək (“to be worth”) and dəyişmək (“to (ex)change”). Cognate with Turkish değer.

From Proto-Turkic *yala. Cognate with
Old Turkic [script needed] (jalγan, “false, fake”),
Turkish yalan (“lie”),
Bashkir ялған (yalğan, “false, fake”),
Kyrgyz жалған (“false, fake”),
Karachay-Balkar джалгъан (calğan, “fake, fictitious”),
Uzbek yolgʻon (“false, fake”),
Uyghur يالغان (yalghan, “lie; false, fake”),
Turkmen ýalan (“false, lie”),
Kazakh жалған (jalğan, “false, spurious”), etc.

From Proto-Common Turkic *kurša- (“to gird”), from Proto-Turkic *kur (“belt, girdle, band, sash”), whence Turkish uçkur. Compare Turkish kuşak, Turkmen guşak, Crimean Tatar кушак (kuşak), and Russian кушак (kušak) (possibly from Kipchak).
Izafet II compound of dil + ön. Calque of Russian переднеязычный (perednejazyčnyj).
